# Tutorial gallery with one-click launch in the Dashboard

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, browsable
surface from which a user can launch a tutorial into their own project with one
click. Launching a notebook tutorial opens a workbench in the user's project
preloaded with the tutorial notebook; launching a pipeline tutorial imports the
tutorial pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines instance.

## Scope

- Gallery view in the Dashboard listing the curated tutorials with enough
  metadata for a user to choose one (title, journey description, level).
- One-click launch mechanics for notebook tutorials: create a workbench in the
  user's project with the tutorial notebook available in it.
- One-click launch mechanics for pipeline tutorials: import the tutorial
  pipeline into the project's Data Science Pipelines instance.
- Launch always targets the user's own project (no shared playground).
- Consumption of the tutorial listing/metadata so the gallery renders the
  curated set maintained by the content owners.
- Availability control through the Dashboard's existing per-component
  configuration mechanism, consistent with how other Dashboard features are
  enabled per deployment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a user with a data science project, when they open the tutorial
  gallery, then the curated tutorials are listed with title and journey
  description (measured by: the gallery renders the curated set in the
  Dashboard).
- Given a notebook tutorial listed in the gallery, when the user clicks launch,
  then a workbench is created in their project containing the tutorial
  notebook (measured by: the workbench reaches Running state and the notebook
  is openable without manual upload steps).
- Given a pipeline tutorial listed in the gallery, when the user clicks launch,
  then the pipeline is imported into the project's Data Science Pipelines
  instance (measured by: the pipeline is visible and runnable in the project).
- End-to-end launch is verified against at least one published notebook
  tutorial and at least one published pipeline tutorial from the curated set.
- The gallery can be enabled or disabled through the Dashboard's existing
  per-component configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project — primary coverage.
- **HLR-2 (P0)**: contributes the launch path that makes the curated tutorials
  one-click launchable (content itself is authored separately).

# Curated notebook tutorials for core user journeys

## Description

This epic authors and maintains the five notebook-based curated tutorials
covering the core getting-started journeys: first workbench, data prep, first
training run, first deployment, and first RAG app. Each tutorial is a tested,
maintained notebook that a new user can launch into their own project from the
tutorial gallery and complete end to end.

## Scope

- Author five notebook tutorials:
  1. First workbench — create and use a first workbench.
  2. Data prep — load and prepare data in a workbench.
  3. First training run — train a first model.
  4. First deployment — deploy a first model for serving.
  5. First RAG app — build a first retrieval-augmented generation app.
- Pin the images and dependencies each tutorial runs on so executions are
  reproducible against the current release.
- Test each tutorial end to end against the current release on a clean project.
- Ensure each notebook tutorial is launchable from the tutorial gallery into a
  user project (the workbench opens with the notebook in place).
- Once the tutorial packaging format is defined, package these tutorials
  according to it (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) and re-run
  validation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a clean user project, when each of the five tutorials is launched and
  followed, then the journey completes without manual fixes (measured by: a
  recorded clean run of each tutorial against the current release).
- Each tutorial runs on pinned images so the run is reproducible (measured by:
  image references are pinned, not floating tags).
- Each notebook tutorial launches from the tutorial gallery into the user's
  project and opens with the notebook in place (measured by: end-to-end launch
  verification with the gallery capability).
- Once the tutorial packaging format is defined, all five tutorials are
  packaged per the format and pass its validation manifest (measured by:
  validation reports pass on the packaged tutorials).
- Tutorial content is technically reviewed for accuracy against the current
  release.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys, each
  tested against the current release — covers the five notebook-based journeys
  (first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, first
  RAG app).
- **HLR-3 (P1)**: these tutorials become the first content packaged in the
  tutorial packaging format once it is defined (adoption is an acceptance
  criterion here, not a blocker).

# Tutorial packaging format

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format — the metadata, pinned-image
conventions, and validation manifest that make a tutorial a versioned,
independently testable unit, decoupled from Dashboard releases. The format is
what allows tutorials to be maintained, versioned, and re-validated on their
own cadence while the Dashboard gallery continues to launch whatever curated
set is current.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial metadata schema (identity, journey, level, content
  location) that the gallery and content authors share.
- Define the pinned-image convention so a tutorial always executes against
  known image versions.
- Define the validation manifest: how a packaged tutorial declares what must
  be tested, and how validation is run and reported.
- Define the versioning scheme so a tutorial can be updated and re-validated
  without a Dashboard release.
- Document the format specification for tutorial authors.
- Demonstrate the format end to end by packaging at least one existing
  published tutorial and running its validation.
- Reach agreement on the format with the teams that consume it (the Dashboard
  gallery owners and the notebook and pipeline tutorial content owners).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The format specification is documented and covers metadata, pinned images,
  and the validation manifest (measured by: a published spec a tutorial author
  can follow).
- A tutorial packaged per the format can be validated independently of a
  Dashboard release (measured by: validation runs on the packaged tutorial and
  reports a pass/fail result).
- A tutorial version bump requires no Dashboard release (measured by: a
  re-versioned, re-validated tutorial with no Dashboard change).
- The format is accepted by the consuming teams — gallery owners and notebook
  and pipeline content owners (measured by: recorded sign-off from each
  consuming team).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)**: A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases — primary coverage.
- **HLR-2 (P0)**: supports the ongoing "maintained, tested" property of the
  curated set; the initially published tutorials are re-packaged into this
  format as an acceptance criterion on their own epics.

# Tutorial gallery documentation

## Description

This epic documents the tutorial gallery for two audiences: users who want to
find and launch a tutorial to reach first success faster, and contributors who
want to add new tutorials to the curated set. It covers using the gallery and
the contribution process for new tutorials.

## Scope

- User documentation for the tutorial gallery: what it is, how to browse the
  curated tutorials, and how to launch a notebook tutorial (workbench) or a
  pipeline tutorial (pipeline import) into your own project.
- Contributor documentation for the tutorial contribution process: the
  tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest),
  how a tutorial is authored, validated, versioned, and submitted for
  inclusion in the curated set.
- Note: contribution process is documented only — no submission tooling is in
  scope for this release (per strategy out-of-scope), and tutorial content is
  not localized.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covers using the gallery: browsing and launching both
  notebook and pipeline tutorials into a user project (measured by: published
  doc topics walk a new user through a first launch).
- Documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials, including
  the packaging format and validation expectations (measured by: a published
  contributor guide a new tutorial author can follow).
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery and
  the published tutorial set (measured by: recorded technical review with no
  open accuracy issues).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)**: Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials — primary coverage.

  strategy itself draws (notebook-based journeys vs. the pipeline journey).
